audit_2026_10_17.verdict: PASS (metadata level) — nightly cadence confirmed at audit, valuations + descriptions present, PDDL license. Dedup design required at connector build (step 3 in PHASE1-PLAN sequence).

coverage_note: City and County of San Francisco (consolidated city-county) — the DBI feed covers the whole jurisdiction. Counts are permits, not feed rows: DBI publishes one row per address/lot a permit touches; each permit is counted once, at its primary address (see dedupe_rule).

dedupe_rule.definition: A 'permit' for San Francisco = one permit_number issued by SF DBI, counted once at its primary address, with its as-reported status, dates, and cost taken from the primary-address record.
dedupe_rule.effect_trailing_12mo: 22,076 feed rows -> 20,170 permits (1,906 sibling rows collapsed, 8.6% of rows).
dedupe_rule.problem: The DBI feed is one row per (permit x address/lot record), not one row per permit. A permit spanning multiple lots or street addresses appears as several rows that are verbatim copies except for address/lot (measured 2026-10-18 on the trailing-12-month issue window: 22,076 rows vs 20,170 distinct permit_number; all 1,906 sibling rows identical to the primary row on status, permit_type, filed_date, issued_date, and cost — so naive row counts overstate permits by 9.4% and naive value sums multiply-count the same project value up to 9x).
dedupe_rule.proof: All-time identity (live API, 2026-10-18): total rows 1,297,058; rows with primary_address_flag='Y' 1,151,033; count(distinct permit_number) 1,151,033 — exactly one primary row per permit_number across the entire dataset, not just the window. In the window pull, sibling rows never disagreed with the primary row on issued_date or filed_date (0 of 20,170 permits), so window membership is consistent: if any row of a permit is in the window, its primary row is too.
dedupe_rule.rule: One published permit = one permit_number, represented by its primary-address record: the pull is restricted to primary_address_flag = 'Y'. Sibling address/lot rows never enter the vault or the DB as separate permits.

field_map.contractor_rule: Dataset publishes NO contractor field and no applicant/owner person fields at all (verified against the full 55-column schema, 2026-10-18) — contractor stays NULL for this source. Never inferred. The pull is additionally column-restricted by pull_select, so no unlisted field can enter our records.
field_map.source_record_id: record_id (the source's per-row id; unique per row. Post-dedupe identity is one record per permit_number — verified at load: COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT permit_number))
field_map.valuation: revised_cost when it is a real figure (> $1), otherwise estimated_cost. Measured 2026-10-18 on the deduped window set: revised_cost carries a $1 placeholder on 2,950 permits; in 120 of those, estimated_cost holds the real figure. Composite coverage: 17,336 of 20,170 permits (86%) carry a real cost; only 30 carry none. TTM sum $3,536,538,582, median real permit $25,904, largest single permit $105,000,000 (3.0% of the total) — no Austin-style stamp duplication after dedupe (dedupe is what makes this sum honest: sibling rows copy the same cost verbatim).
field_map.work_type_source: permit_type_definition + description + reroof / fire_only_permit flags (dedicated classifier pass: trades.classify_sf_trade)
